title: Your agents lack context: Here's how to fix "You're absolutely right!" — Brandon Waselnuk, Unblocked
talk_summary: Brandon argues agents fail not from intelligence but from missing organizational context, and proposes a context engine that ingests source systems, resolves conflicts, personalizes relevance, and returns token-optimized context. He offers concrete open-source patterns: deterministic GitHub expertise graphs, repo-rule indexing/deduplication, and relational querying beyond RAG.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of letting each agent session rediscover repo/issue/PR context via search, inject a compact task-specific context bundle at run start.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it took about 21 million tokens without and then 18, or sorry, 10.8 million tokens with it.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use deterministic analysis of commits/reviews to build an experts graph showing who works where and who reviews whom; optionally LLM-label teams.
takeaways.evidence_quote: using all deterministic programming, goes over your GitHub and understands who works on your team

takeaways.what_they_do: Discover all rules files across repo, check duplicates/severity conflicts, and expose a deduped index for retrieval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: discover all the places your team has written rules files, checks them all

takeaways.technique: Relational query interface over work artifacts
takeaways.what_they_do: Beyond vector RAG, let agents discover a schema and write deterministic queries for relational questions like open PRs by author/time/topic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Rag cannot answer that question alone. You need queries.

takeaways.what_they_do: When sources disagree, prefer recent authoritative signals over old architecture docs; don't stop at first retrieved fact.
takeaways.evidence_quote: an old architecture diagram and last night's Slack convo with the CTO, which one is right?

takeaways.technique: Avoid curated context trap; auto-generate from source systems
takeaways.what_they_do: Hand-maintained markdown context repos rot and need an omnipotent curator; instead ingest and index from source systems automatically.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that repo is going to rot just like all the other docs you wrote down
